title: Routine Newborn Care & Normal Findings
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Assessment, Exam Timeline & Routine Care
AAP / Bright Futures newborn care; AAP 2022 hyperbilirubinemia (pre-discharge bilirubin risk assessment)

changelog.change: Initial entry — normal vitals, the routine-care order, the three exams, normal findings not to mistake for pathology, and the pre-discharge checklist.

purpose: Normal term-newborn parameters, the routine-care sequence, and the findings that are normal variants — so a benign finding doesn't trigger an unnecessary workup and a real one isn't missed.

items: Dry, remove wet linen, skin-to-skin or warmer.
Early breastfeeding; 8–12 feeds / 24 h on demand.
Vitamin K₁ 0.5–1 mg IM within 6 h of birth — prevents vitamin K deficiency bleeding.
Eye prophylaxis: erythromycin 0.5% ophthalmic ointment (gonococcal ophthalmia).
Umbilical cord care: keep clean and dry.
Glucose monitoring in at-risk infants (IDM, SGA / LGA, preterm, symptomatic).
Monitor output: first void by 24 h, first meconium by 48 h.

rows: Apgar, gestational age, anomalies / birth injury
Complete systematic — jaundice, seizures, vomiting, cyanosis
Metabolic screen, vaccinations, hearing screen, red reflex

body.text: Normal — do NOT mistake for pathology

Skull moulding · breast hypertrophy (maternal hormone withdrawal) · vaginal bleeding / mucoid discharge in girls (pseudomenses, first week) · liver edge palpable 1–2 cm below the costal margin · palpable spleen tip · meconium in the first stool · erythema toxicum · milia · Epstein pearls.

items: Vaccinations per schedule (at minimum the Hep B birth dose).
Document the red reflex (rules out cataract, retinoblastoma).
Pre-discharge bilirubin risk assessment (AAP 2022 — TSB/TcB plotted on the hour-specific nomogram).
